neighbours.label: the predicate of an escalation or change of degree ('even more', 'gets more complicated', 'a bit trickier', 'goes out the window when')
fire: When the rain started, the fans sang even louder than before.
The debate becomes far more heated once money enters the picture.
Driving gets a lot trickier when the roads freeze overnight.
Her second novel was even better than her first.
All those careful plans went out the window when the baby arrived.
Prices climbed still higher as the shortage dragged on.
The puzzle gets much harder in the final chapter.
Our worries grew even deeper when the letter never came.
quiet: We ordered more chairs for the party on Saturday.
The debate took place in a small hall downtown.
Driving to the coast takes about three hours.
Her second novel was published in the spring.
She opened the window to let in some fresh air.
Prices are listed on the board next to the door.
The puzzle has five hundred pieces and a picture of a lighthouse.
The letter arrived on Tuesday with a blue stamp.

notes: Card: ' more' in 'cheered even more loudly', 'goes out the window', 'more interesting when', 'a bit trickier', 'hung in the balance'. Probe: comparative escalations fired (~0.5-0.6), quantity 'more apples' silent, 'hung in the balance' weak.
